questions.q: A beachfront residence is planned on a narrow lot with unobstructed sea views as the primary design objective. Which structural concept best supports the architectural intent?
o: Utilize load-bearing masonry walls perpendicular to the shoreline to handle the wind loads.
Implement a dense grid of closely spaced columns to minimize beam depths and maximize floor-to-ceiling height.
Utilize a structural system with longer spans to reduce the frequency of vertical supports.
Incorporate perimeter shear walls along the viewing deck to provide maximum structural stiffness.
questions.n: Increasing the span length minimizes columns and vertical members, thereby maximizing unobstructed panoramic openings facing the sea.

questions.q: A residence is elevated above grade to address potential coastal flooding. From a structural standpoint, which consideration becomes more critical?
o: Ensuring the elevated structure can adequately resist overturning and lateral forces.
Maximizing the flexibility of the primary floor diaphragms to allow for building sway.
Increasing the dead load of the roof system to resist downward atmospheric forces.
Reducing the cross-sectional area of foundation footings to minimize subsoil friction.
questions.n: Elevating the structure exposes its base to hydrodynamic forces, storm surges, and high coastal winds, making overturning resistance and lateral stability paramount.

questions.q: The architect proposes large glazed openings facing the ocean. Which structural concept is most appropriate?
o: Decrease the story height to automatically increase the overall stiffness of the glass panels.
Compensate for the reduction in wall stiffness by strengthening adjacent structural elements.
Substitute standard structural concrete framing with lightweight steel trusses across the entire envelope.
Utilize non-load-bearing partitions directly behind the glass panels to distribute wind pressure.
questions.n: Replacing rigid wall areas with large glazing reduces the building's lateral stiffness; nearby elements like columns, beams, or boundary frames must be strengthened to absorb those displaced forces.

questions.q: The development of Casa Manila is an example of which approach in architectural conservation?
questions.n: Casa Manila is a reproduction colonial house designed to serve a new contemporary public function as a museum and commercial venue, making it an example of adaptive reuse.

questions.q: What is the primary challenge of retrofitting heritage buildings?
o: Sourcing matching decorative paints from local modern paint manufacturers.
Calculating the precise total weight of original handmade clay brick masonry.
Finding original blueprints in the archives of the building's original architect.
Difficult to insert new utility systems in old structures
questions.n: Heritage buildings lack the built-in conduits, chases, and plenums required for modern MEPFS systems, making utility integration without damage highly complex.

questions.q: Retrofitting involves which of the following?
o: Total teardown and replacement with modern materials mimicking the old aesthetic.
Preserving the building's original design without changes
Adding completely new and contrasting architectural wings to expand total floor area.
Demolishing internal structures completely while keeping only the external skin intact.
questions.n: Retrofitting systematically updates elements to improve performance while strictly retaining the original design intent and architectural appearance.

questions.q: What is the common debate between heritage preservation and modernization?
o: Zoning Regulations vs. Building Code Compliance
Private Ownership Rights vs. Public Utility Routing
questions.n: The fundamental tension lies between maximizing land value through modern high-density development and protecting the cultural value of historical heritage.

questions.q: How can a balance between preservation and modernization be achieved?
questions.n: Adaptive reuse allows historical buildings to remain functional and financially viable in the modern economy by changing their internal function while safeguarding their historic skin.

questions.q: A single accessible entrance for all users is an example of which Universal Principle of Design?
questions.n: Equitable use means the design is useful and marketable to people with diverse abilities, ensuring identical means of use for everyone to avoid stigmatization.

questions.q: When a space is easily adaptable to any use or function, which principle is being applied?
o: Size and Space for Approach and Use
questions.n: Flexibility in use demands that the design accommodates a wide range of individual preferences and abilities through adaptability.

questions.q: When you design a space with color coding so that even without text or signage, the building is still usable and navigable, what principle is being applied?
questions.n: Simple and intuitive design eliminates unnecessary complexity, ensuring usage is straightforward and easily understood regardless of literacy or language skills.

questions.q: Railings and zocalo that are designed to accommodate ease of use are examples of which principle?
questions.n: Designing railings and proper base profiles (zocalos) prevents accidents, guides movement safely, and minimizes the physical hazards or consequences of missteps.

questions.q: Panic doors that are not heavy and use lever-type handles are an example of which principle?
o: Size and Space for Approach and Use
questions.n: Lever handles and lightweight assemblies allow users to actuate and pass through doors comfortably with minimal gripping, twisting, or strength.

questions.q: What is the minimum length of a bath and toilet?
questions.n: The absolute minimum legal length required to satisfy minimum clearances for a standard compact bath and toilet stall configuration is 1.2 meters.

questions.q: What is the minimum ceiling height for natural ventilation?
questions.n: Under the National Building Code of the Philippines (PD 1096), rooms intended for human habitation utilizing natural ventilation must have a minimum ceiling height of 2.7 meters.

questions.q: What is the minimum ceiling height for artificial ventilation?
questions.n: According to PD 1096, when a room is provided with an artificial or mechanical ventilation system, the minimum code-compliant ceiling height is reduced to 2.4 meters.

questions.q: What is the minimum ceiling height for a mezzanine?
questions.n: The National Building Code mandates that a mezzanine floor must have a clear ceiling height of not less than 1.8 meters measured from its floor to the ceiling above.

questions.q: Ventilation or vent shafts shall have a horizontal cross-sectional area of not less than how many square meters for every meter of height of the shaft?
questions.n: The code mandates that vertical ventilation shafts must maintain a minimum cross-sectional area proportion of 0.1 square meters for every linear meter of total shaft height.

questions.q: What does PABX stand for?
questions.n: PABX stands for Private Automatic Branch Exchange, which is an automatic telephone switching system within a private enterprise.

questions.q: What is the common telephone cable used in the Philippines?
questions.n: RJ11 is the standard physical connector and registered jack configuration widely deployed for typical 2-to-4 wire analog telephone connections in the Philippines.

questions.q: What is the common ethernet cable used in the Philippines?
questions.n: RJ45 is the standard 8-pin modular connector interface used globally and locally to terminate twisted-pair Ethernet data cables.

questions.q: Which of the following is a brand for security systems?
questions.n: Visonic is a globally recognized manufacturer of wireless home security systems, intruder alarms, and safety monitoring tech widely specified in the Philippines.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a floor raise system?
o: To completely seal structural joints against high coastal water table pressures.
To artificially raise the ceiling height of the story below it.
To increase the overall dead weight and structural mass of the building.
Easily use of floor box without cutting the floor slab
questions.n: A raised floor system creates an underfloor plenum space, allowing electrical, data, and mechanical lines to route directly to floor boxes without damaging the structural concrete slab.

questions.q: How many live wires are in a 3-phase system?
questions.n: A alternating current 3-phase electrical distribution system utilizes exactly 3 active, energized ungrounded 'live' phase conductors.

questions.q: How many live wires are in a 1-phase system?
questions.n: A standard standard-voltage single-phase circuit utilizes exactly 1 hot or 'live' wire paired with a neutral return path.
